Issue Title: Catastrophic Mobile Core Web Vitals: LCP 19.4s & Speed Index 17.6s
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: While synthetic tools report an initial FCP of 0.8s on the empty shell, real mobile visitors must wait 19.4 seconds before the Largest Contentful Paint (hero image and headline) renders. The Speed Index is 17.6 seconds, reflecting an excruciatingly sluggish visual completion rate. The page triggers 3.7 seconds of blocking main-thread JavaScript execution and downloads an enormous 4,429 KiB (4.4 MB) uncompressed payload, causing massive mobile user abandonment.

Issue Title: Absence of a Valid Robots.txt File (Nginx SPA HTML Rewrite Trap)
Affected Scope: https://storiai.ai/robots.txt (Returns HTTP 200 with text/html SPA shell)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Nginx's blanket SPA rewrite rule intercepts requests for /robots.txt and serves the React index.html. Search engines requesting /robots.txt parse HTML markup as syntax errors, which can cause unpredictable crawling behavior, default to unrestricted crawling of sensitive private routes (/dashboard, /account-settings, /orders), or block indexing altogether.

Issue Title: Complete Absence of an XML Sitemap for Search Engine Discovery
Affected Scope: https://storiai.ai/sitemap.xml (Returns HTTP 200 with text/html SPA shell)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: No XML sitemap exists on the domain. Because internal navigation links are buried inside client-side JavaScript components, search engines have zero crawlable discovery pathways to find and index critical marketing pages such as /about, /pricing, /faq, /contact, and /stories-across-languages.

Issue Title: SPA Catch-All Soft 404 / Phantom URL Trap on All Non-Existent Routes
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The Nginx configuration (try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;) returns HTTP 200 OK for every non-existent, mistyped, or deleted URL. Because the server never emits HTTP 404 Not Found or HTTP 410 Gone status codes, search engine crawlers interpret broken links and typo URLs as valid pages, resulting in severe Soft 404 penalties and crawl budget exhaustion.

Issue Title: Split Indexing & Hostname Canonical Dilution (www vs non-www Both 200 OK)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Both https://www.storiai.ai/ and https://storiai.ai/ respond with HTTP 200 OK independently without a 301 permanent redirect consolidating them. Combined with the absence of canonical tags, search engines treat the www and non-www versions as two competing duplicate websites, splitting domain authority and ranking equity.

Issue Title: Complete Absence of Canonical Link Tags Across All Domain Routes
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The HTML shell completely omits canonical link elements. In a Single Page Application where URLs can be accessed via trailing slashes, query parameters, or alternative hostnames, the absence of canonical tags leaves search engines to guess which version to index, leading to index fragmentation.

Issue Title: Missing Server-Side Caching Headers (Cache-Control: None on 4.4MB Payloads)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Nginx sends no Cache-Control or max-age headers for static JavaScript and CSS assets. Lighthouse identifies an estimated cache savings of 4,633 KiB on Desktop and 4,323 KiB on Mobile. Every time a visitor navigates between pages or returns to the site, their browser must revalidate or re-download multi-megabyte bundles, destroying repeat user experience.

Issue Title: Zero HTTP Compression on 1.52MB Unminified JavaScript Bundles
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Nginx transmits JavaScript and CSS files without Gzip or Brotli compression (Content-Encoding: None). The main application chunk (App-XFfRbN91.js) is served as a massive 1.52 MB raw text file. Standard Brotli compression would reduce this file by over 75% to approximately 350 KB, immediately resolving the primary network bottleneck causing the 19.4s mobile LCP.

Issue Title: Missing Meta Descriptions Across All Marketing & Informational Pages
Affected Scope: Site-wide (<meta name='description' content='' /> in raw HTML shell)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The raw HTML shell contains a hardcoded empty meta description tag. In search engine results, Google is forced to either auto-generate snippets from fragmented client-side text or display empty snippets, resulting in depressed click-through rates (CTR) on branded and commercial searches.

Issue Title: Minimal Hardcoded Page Title ('StoriAI' - 7 Characters / 59 Pixels)
Affected Scope: Site-wide (<title>StoriAI</title> across all URLs in raw HTML shell)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The title tag is hardcoded in the HTML shell as just 'StoriAI' (7 characters / 59 pixels). It fails to communicate core value propositions (e.g. 'Personalized AI Children's Bedtime Stories') or secondary keywords, wasting Google's 561-pixel desktop / 60-character snippet allowance across all 61 routes.

Issue Title: Complete Absence of OpenGraph and Twitter Social Share Cards
Affected Scope: Site-wide (0 og:* and 0 twitter:* tags in HTML shell)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The HTML shell contains zero OpenGraph (og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url) and zero Twitter Card tags. When links to StoriAI are shared on WhatsApp, LinkedIn, X, Facebook, or Slack, no visual preview card or description generates, severely impeding viral and social user acquisition.

Issue Title: Complete Absence of Schema.org Structured Data (0 JSON-LD Entities)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The website provides zero Schema.org structured data. Search engines cannot programmatically identify StoriAI as a SoftwareApplication / WebApplication, recognize its subscription pricing, understand its Organization entity, or ingest the extensive FAQs embedded in the React code for SERP rich results.

Issue Title: Trailing Slash Duplicate Content Proliferation Without 301 Consolidation
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Both trailing slash and non-trailing slash URL variations return HTTP 200 OK independently without a 301 redirect enforcing a single format. Combined with www and non-www variations, every single page on the site can be resolved at 4 separate URLs without canonical consolidation.

Issue Title: Leaked Port 443 in HTTP-to-HTTPS 301 Redirect Headers
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: HTTP requests to http://storiai.ai/ and http://www.storiai.ai/ return a 301 redirect with an explicit port 443 in the Location header (https://storiai.ai:443/). While modern browsers normalize the port, legacy crawlers and proxy servers treat the explicit port as a distinct URL string, causing unnecessary redirect hops.

Issue Title: 3.7 Seconds of Blocking Main-Thread JavaScript Execution on Mobile
Affected Scope: Site-wide (Lighthouse Diagnostic: Minimize main-thread work - 3.7 s)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Lighthouse flags 3.7 seconds of continuous main-thread JavaScript execution on mobile CPU, identifying 4 long tasks and 1,133 KiB of unused JavaScript in the initial bundle. Compiling Redux store slices, Material-UI Emotion styling engines, and unused routes on the initial load freezes the browser UI and drives up the Speed Index to 17.6s.

Issue Title: Default Boilerplate Web App Manifest Leaking Development Metadata
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The web app manifest contains unedited default development boilerplate: 'TypeScript + React + Redux + MUI + RRD + ESLint + Prettier => Boilerplate'. This leaks internal development stack details to search engines and PWA browsers instead of describing the production children's storytelling product.

Issue Title: Missing Explicit Image Dimensions (width/height) Triggering Layout Shifts
Affected Scope: Site-wide (Lighthouse Diagnostic: Image elements do not have explicit width and height)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: Hero and illustrative images (hero-home.webp, avatar illustrations, book covers) are inserted into the DOM without explicit HTML width and height attributes or CSS aspect ratios, causing layout instability during client-side rendering.

Issue Title: Missing Security Response Headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The Nginx server completely omits Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff), Content-Security-Policy (CSP), and Referrer-Policy headers. This exposes visitors to MIME-sniffing, clickjacking in malicious iframes, and man-in-the-middle protocol downgrade attacks.

Issue Title: Server Software Footprint and Version Exposure (nginx/1.31.8)
Observed Defect & Commercial Consequence: The HTTP response headers publicly broadcast the exact web server software and version (Server: nginx/1.31.8). Exposing software version banners provides automated vulnerability scanners and malicious actors with intelligence on known CVEs.
